newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Inassit approves capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Inassit approves capital increase.

text.p: Shareholders in Inassit, the company which will take over 60 percent of struggling Banco Napoli, have approved plans for it to raise its capital to 100 billion lire from the current 600 million.
The company, which is 51 percent owned by Italian insurer INA and 49 percent by Banco Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL), has also changed its name to Banco di Napoli Holding Spa, a statement from INA said.
At a shareholders' meeting, the company nominated the new board which will include Lino Benassi, Davide Croff, Giancarlo Giannini, BNL president Mario Sarcinelli and INA chairman Sergio Siglienti.
The board will nominate the chairman, vice president and managing director at its next meeting.

INA and BNL have agreed jointly to acquire Banco di Napoli, which is the largest in southern Italy, after the Italian Treasury offered 60 percent of it for sale as part of rescue operation after it clocked up record losses of 3.16 trillion lire in 1995.
